source_document.body:
2026 Paris Motor Show • Chinese Brand AITO Plans 2027 European Launch
Ford Order Guide Confirms 2027 Ranger Drops 2.7L EcoBoost V6, Detuned 3.0L EcoBoost V6 Replaces It
28 photos
Photo: Ford / edited
Ford is giving Ranger buyers a good reason to skip the Raptor entirely. As per the 2027 order guide, the XLT and Lariat are dropping the optional 2.7-liter EcoBoost V6 for the 3.0-liter EcoBoost V6 that has already replaced the 2.7 in the mechanically similar Bronco and the F-150 pickup truck.
The order guide does not offer any kind of maximum output numbers for the newcomer, although the Bronco's advertised figures are believed to carry over. In optimal conditions, the detuned version of the Raptor's engine makes a very respectable 380 horsepower and 440 pound-feet (597 Newton-meters) of twist. Similarly, a 10-speed automatic tranny will have to suffice.
If the Ranger follows the Bronco's lead , the 3.0-liter EcoBoost twin-turbo V6 would amount to more than 0.3 additional liters of displacement. Against the outgoing 2.7, the 3.0 gives the midsizer an extra 65 horsepower and 40 pound-feet (54 Newton-meters) at full chatter, making the XLT a very appealing yet understated truck.
You wouldn't need the higher equipment group, either. Attached below, the order guide lists the new sixer for both the 300A and 301A groups, along with the Lariat's 500A specification. Four-wheel drive comes with the 3.0 by default, whereas the 2.3 remains the standard choice across the XLT and Lariat. XL buyers stick with four cylinders, though, as expected from a work-oriented trim level.
The XLT's 301A equipment group includes power adjustments for both front seats, heated front seats, and a power-sliding rear window. The guide further leaves room to build the sort of pickup that interests prospective customers who read a vehicle past wheel finishes and the paint job. Add the FX4 package, and you get an electronic locking rear diff, off-road shocks, a steel bash plate, and extra underbody protection.
Photo: Ford FX4 also sweetens the deal with Mud/Ruts and Sand drive mods, and the finishing touch is Trail Control. New optional rocker rails with hoop-style steps require the FX4 package. All in all, that combo gives the larger V6 a very tasteful supporting cast without pretending that lesser Rangers have turned into undercover Raptors.
Raptor customers are presented with trick dampers from the folks at Fox, locking front and rear axles, a nicer rear suspension setup, and Baja mode for good measure. Lariat and lesser models retain rear leaf springs in lieu of the Raptor's Watts-link design. The coil-sprung rear suspension of the Raptor improves high-speed stability off the beaten path and suspension travel, the trade-offs being maximum payload and towing capacities.
The order guide clearly states the Raptor's engine is a high-output affair, but even though it develops more than 400 ponies on premium-grade dinosaur juice, the Raptor-grade mill makes the very same 440 pound-feet of peak torque as the detuned 3.0 of non-Raptor grades. The cheapest Ranger for 2027 in the US market adds dual-zone electronic climate control, a 12-inch center display, Intersection Assist, and Lane Keeping Assist as standard.
Ford's Connectivity Package is standard as well, and it includes a one-year subscription. Ford Co-Pilot360 2.0 becomes standard on the XLT. No fewer than five optional packages have been deleted for 2027. In their place, Ford offers the Bronze Appearance Package, a graphics delete for said package, a graphics delete for the Black Appearance Package, and the Luxury Package.
The 17-inch black steelies are gone in favor of aluminum wheels. When it comes to paint options, Neptune Blue enters the scene to the detriment of Velocity Blue and Carbonized Gray. Lastly, the Space Gray interior theme replaces Sandstone.
